content_blocks.text: Here in the M&R procurement team, we have been reminiscing fondly about our 10-year relationship with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 – especially since there are now only 7 days to go until it is finally time to say goodbye (for new procurements started on or after 24 February at least!)
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: This moment has been five years in the making - since the Green Paper was first introduced in December 2020 - and we have turned to poems, songs and even eulogies to mark the transition – who said procurement lawyers were not creative?
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Of course, there has been such a flurry of activity from the Cabinet Office this week in relation to the Procurement Act 2023 that you might not have had a spare moment to reflect on the passing of the PCRs.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: National Procurement Policy Statement
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: The new National Procurement Policy Statement – long awaited and the stated cause of the need to delay the October 2024 implementation date - was published last week, meaning authorities now have a clearer sense of what it is that they will need to “have regard to” when running a procurement.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Procurement Act 2023 PPNs
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: We also had first sight of some new “ Procurement Act 2023 PPNs ” - PPN 001 on setting targets for SME and VCSE spend for central government authorities, and PPN 002 providing an update to the Social Value Model.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Under PPN 01, from 1 April 2025 central government authorities need to set a three-year target for SME spend, and from 1 April 2026 a two-year target for VCSE spend.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Under PPN 02, the Social Value Model has been updated to align with the National Procurement Policy Statement – presumably making the adoption of the Model a good route for an authority – including non-central government if desired - to demonstrate the required “having regard to”. The new Social Value Model is mandatory from October 2025 but can be applied sooner.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Payments Compliance Guidance
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: The final pieces of official government guidance have been published, including on Payments Compliance Notices (together with confirmation that the requirement at section 69 of the Act to publish the Payments Compliance Notice is not coming into force just yet but will follow later this year).
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: It is worth noting, though, that section 68 is coming into force next week – so it will be an implied term of all contracts under the Act that the authority must pay within 30 days of a valid and undisputed invoice. This obligation is then passed down the subcontracting chain thanks to section 73.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: The Procurement Act 2023 (Consequential and Other Amendments) Regulations 2025
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: If you were feeling pleased that you had begun to get to grips with the Act and the Procurement Regulations 2024, you may need to pause, because also last week, a further piece of secondary legislation was finalised – the Procurement Act 2023 (Consequential and Other Amendments) Regulations 2025 .
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: These 2025 Regulations make further clarifying amendments to various pieces of legislation – particularly the Procurement Regulations 2024 around which KPIs need to be published and reported on. The amendments are helpfully summarised in the explanatory memorandum ; you will want to make sure that you are always looking at the updated version of each piece of legislation under the Act.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Don’t Panic!
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: There are only 7 days to go until implementation of the Act but if you are feeling underprepared, don’t panic!
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Take a look at our 5 in 25 webinar on implementation for our summary of how the land lies at implementation.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Don’t try to access the new Central Digital Platform (FTS) over the weekend, as it will be unavailable from 1730 on 21 February to 2359 on 23 February to allow the updates to the new platform to be made.
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: Once you are underway with your first Procurement Act 2023 procurement, do explore our Procurement Portal which has been updated for the new Act and includes some helpful new tools and information:
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: our Notices Generator – allows you to input the contract type, value and award process and it tells you which notices you need to publish for your procurement;
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: our Procurement Act 2024 Standstill Calculator – calculates the appropriate standstill period under the Act;
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: our Notices Infographic – a helpful flowchart (produced in partnership with Tussell ) to guide you through the notice publication process;
heading_path: PPNs, Payment Compliance, Procurement Policy Statement, and implementation – don’t panic …

content_blocks.text: our series of 5 in 25 webinars on the Act - you can find recordings of all our webinars plus a list of the Q&A raised at each. If you’d like to be invited to our future webinars (the next one is on 22 nd May 2025) then you can register your interest here .
